Gold Line Construction  design and construction  efforts for the Metro Gold Line light rail project. In
  preparation  for work at the grade crossings,  all sewer and storm drainpipes
  were inspected  and several  structural  deficiencies  were noted. While these

  construction  of the Gold Line light rail project in La Verne. Recommended

  400, 000 from the storm drain fund.  Approved  as recommended.

7.  Re- opening  of  City Parks  Mayor Hepburn asked if there was any public comment or phone
  communications regarding the re- opening of parks.

  There was none.

  Public Comments regarding re- opening of the parks that were received via
  email and shared with the City Council are attached.

  Mayor Hepburn stated that he requested placing on the Agenda the re- opening
  of City Parks for discussion. He reported that he has received numerous
  emails and phones calls from residents requesting that the City parks be re-
  opened.  He stated he understands the importance of following the Los
  Angeles County Health Department COVID- 19 guidelines to keep the
  community safe, but it was also important that children and teens be allowed to
  enjoy the outside city recreational facilities for exercise and to expend energy,
  especially now with distance learning. He moved that all the closed parks
  signs be removed immediately and to re- open the basketball courts, skate
  park, fields, playgrounds,  and the aquatic  center.  He stated  that families
  should be able to enjoy the parks without having the Police kicking them out.
  Mayor Hepburn also was not happy with the cancellation of the September 03,
  2020 Youth Sports Committee  because  of the anticipated  residents who would
  be attending to voice their disapproval of the closed City recreational facilities.

  The City Council discussed the pros and cons of re- opening the playgrounds,
  basketball courts, aquatic center, skate park and the fields. They also
  discussed the permitted uses allowed in parks by individual families and the
  importance of following the Los Angeles County Health COVID- 19 guidelines
  to keep the community safe.

  City Manager Russi reported on the City' s Youth Sports Group Status of Use
  and the Youth Sports Protocols. He explained how youth sports groups could
  submit a plan to restart with the City that follows the Los Angeles County
  Health Re- opening Protocols.

  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Davis and action failed by a vote of 1-
  4 ( Lau, Crosby, Davis, and Carder voted No ) to take down all closed City park
  signs and to re- open the City fields, playgrounds, basketball courts, aquatic
  center and the skate park immediately.  Motion failed.
   City Council Minutes, Tuesday, September 8, 2020, Page 5

8.  Public  Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone  communication.

  There  was  none.

9.  Council  Comments  Council Member Crosby stated he appreciates everything the City does.

  Council Member Lau thanked everyone for the input.  She urged residents to
  watch the video presentation on the fire study on the City' s website and to
  send in their comments. She stated that this was challenging times for
  everyone due to COVID- 19 and that the Council is doing their best to serve the
  community.

  Mayor Pro Tem Carder  reported  on Hillcrest  Homes  and the residents.  She
  spoke about the importance of checking on senior citizens because many
  need  assistance.

  Council Member Davis reminded everyone of the upcoming Election in
  November and to VOTE.  In addition, he urged residents to complete the
  census and be counted. He urged everyone to take care during these
  challenging times due to COVD- 19. He thanked the La Verne Fire Department
  for their professionalism and the great job putting out a fire when they quickly
  responded  to an incident at his home.

  Mayor Hepburn stated that the City Council needs input from residents on the
  fire study. He asked everyone to watch out for children and to reach out to
  family and friends during these challenging times due to COVID- 19. He urged
  residents to shop La Verne.

Good evening,

As a resident of La Verne for the last 6 years, and a local resident for 40 years, I have never been more disappointed in
the people who are supposedly in charge of our city, than I am tonight. I cannot believe that we had 4 city council
members vote NO to open our parks up for kids when if this council actually took the time to listen to their residents, you
would realize this should have been a 5- 0 YES vote.

Your actions are teaching our kids that it is not safe to play in the city that they live in. Is that the message you want
received? Making posts on Facebook, asking our families to call the police if we see kids on a playground, is ridiculous
and is no way to restore faith in our families

Your actions are forcing our families to leave La Verne to play outside which is essential to their health and well being.
When we leave the city to play at the park, to practice and play games, we also tend to dine and shop in the city we are in
which is taking money away from our local businesses. They are struggling enough, why don' t you create safe actions that
will encourage families to stay in the city every day?

The fact that you will approve a paid skills class that the city financially benefits from and open the parks for that, all the
while denying free play for families, proves the point that you are not making this decision in the best interest of our city
and the residents who live here. When your Parks and Rec director Chad immediately cancels a meeting because he
 hears that residents are showing up to express their concerns, and hides once again behind LA county guidelines, this
just reinforces the message that you don' t want to hear from your residents. Where there is a will, there is a way

Our families  need  you  to listen  to your residents,  make  decisions  with your residents  in mind - not just for your own
personal agenda and we need you to take a stand to support our families. I look forward to hearing from the 4 of you who
voted no, you definitely have a lot of explaining to do to the residents of La Verne.

A very concerned resident,
